title: Frustrating Google Home bug refuses to add items to your shopping lists in Keep
summary: Another day, another Google Home bug.
body: TL;DR Some Google Home users are facing a bug where the voice assistant refuses to add items to their Google Keep lists. While not all users appear to be facing this issue, it appears widespread enough for Google to take notice. Meanwhile, a quick look at Google Home settings suggests that access to notes & lists using a voice assistant may have been removed. It feels like we’re reporting on a Google Home bug or a fix almost every other day. Only today, users received some good news following reports of devices refusing to set alarms over voice commands. Sadly, those good times aren’t going to last, and it now looks like yet another function is being impacted by a similar glitch, as some people are seemingly unable to add items to their lists on Google Keep using Google Home voice commands. In a series of complaints on Reddit, including one from Friday, a user claims the voice assistant recognizes their commands perfectly well, but refuses to add items to the list . For instance, if the person asks one of their Google Home devices to “add x to list xyz,” the assistant might respond by saying how many items are on that list, while refusing to add any new items.

title: The next wide-screen foldable may have just leaked in real-world images
summary: New leaked images offer a closer look at Xiaomi’s mysterious wide-screen foldable.
body: TL;DR Xiaomi’s next foldable has leaked, showing a wide inner display and a design that closely resembles the company’s own HyperOS 4 teaser. The XRing O3 will power the device, with a 10-core CPU, Arm’s new G2-Ultra NX GPU, and eye-catching performance claims. The Xiaomi 18 Fold launches in September, but key details such as global availability, pricing, and dimensions remain unknown. Xiaomi’s XRing O3 chipset has already made headlines with some seriously ambitious performance claims, but the chip’s first phone may be just as interesting. Xiaomi has confirmed that the 3nm processor will debut in the Xiaomi 18 Fold next month, and now leaked images appear to show the company’s upcoming foldable in the flesh. The images, which Digital Chat Station (DCS) shared on Weibo , show a book-style foldable with a wide inner display similar to the Galaxy Z Fold 8 , relatively thick bezels, and a punch-hole selfie camera near the upper-right corner. One image also shows the rear of the device, including a large camera module, but it doesn’t reveal enough to say much about its hardware.

title: Nothing unveils Nothing OS 5.0 built on Android 17, but there’s bad news for older phones

body: TL;DR Nothing has announced Nothing OS 5.0, bringing a massive overhaul featuring the Geist typeface, translucent software layering, dynamic wallpaper-tinted adaptive themes, and dedicated apps for both the Glyph Interface and Essential Apps Builder. The update also introduces Android 17 platform features such as split notification and Quick Settings panels, cross-platform Quick Share with iOS, enhanced privacy indicators, and more. Open Beta testing for the Nothing Phone 3 starts tomorrow, with a full stable release expected in mid-October. However, Phone 1, Phone 2, and CMF Phone 1 will not receive the update. Nothing has officially revealed Nothing OS 5.0, detailing the next major evolution of its custom Android skin. Built on top of Android 17 , the platform update brings a visual design overhaul, expanded lock screen personalization, new first-party widgets, and tighter system-level integration with the Glyph Interface. Following an announcement teased on X , Nothing published a detailed breakdown of the new features and the design evolution on its community forums.

title: The next flagship Snapdragon will be the first 5GHz smartphone chip, and here’s why you should care
summary: Thought today's smartphone CPUs had high clock speeds? Qualcomm will make a giant leap forward next month.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority TL;DR Qualcomm has announced the first details for its next-generation Snapdragon flagship processor. The new processor has a 5GHz CPU, making it the first smartphone CPU to reach this milestone. A new “FlexCache” architecture also delivers more performance improvements. Qualcomm has teased the arrival of two Snapdragon 8 Elite series chips at its Snapdragon Summit next month. Now, the company has revealed the first details about its new silicon, and it might have an impressive CPU. Qualcomm has officially detailed the CPU for its next-generation Snapdragon processor, and this is the first smartphone CPU to reach 5GHz. That’s an impressive achievement on paper and comes after the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy reached a peak speed of 4.74GHz. The firm’s own graphic shows that you can expect two 5GHz CPU cores along with six “performance” cores running at an unspecified frequency.

body: الإيفواري يتطلع للألقاب أكد الإيفواري يان ديوماندي، أحدث صفقات ريال مدريد، سعادته الكبيرة بالانضمام إلى النادي الملكي، مشددًا على رغبته في تقديم كل ما لديه من أجل مساعدة الفريق على حصد الألقاب خلال الموسم الحالي. وجاءت تصريحات ديوماندي في  مؤتمر صحفي عقب إتمام مراسم الترحيب الرسمية به في مدينة ريال مدريد، وتوقيع عقده الذي يمتد حتى عام 2033. وقال ديوماندي: "أنا فخور، لأن هذا هو أكبر نادٍ في العالم. في الوقت الحالي، الجميع يحلم باللعب مع ريال مدريد، وأنا سأقدم كل ما لدي". وأعرب اللاعب الشاب عن سعادته بالعمل تحت قيادة المدرب البرتغالي جوزيه مورينيو، مؤكدًا أنه يعتبره الأفضل في العالم، إلى جانب اللعب بجوار مجموعة من أبرز نجوم كرة القدم. يمكنكم مناقشة الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات "كووورة" وأضاف: "أن يدربني أفضل مدرب في العالم، وأن أشارك غرفة الملابس مع أفضل اللاعبين في العالم، أمر مذهل". ولم يضع ديوماندي سقفًا لطموحاته مع ريال مدريد، حيث كشف عن هدفه في المنافسة بقوة على أهم بطولتين خلال الموسم، وهما الدوري الإسباني ودوري أبطال أوروبا. وقال المهاجم الإيفواري: "رؤية كل هذه البطولات تجعلك متحمسًا للفوز بلقب آخر. من المثير جدًا المنافسة في الدوري الإسباني ودوري أبطال أوروبا من أجل الفوز بهما، ولماذا لا نبدأ من هذا العام؟". ويبلغ ديوماندي 19 عامًا، وانضم إلى ريال مدريد قادمً…

title: Galaxy S26 series gets sixth One UI 9 beta release, but when is the stable update coming?
summary: The latest 851MB update targets several UI and routine issues for global users ahead of the stable launch.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has released the sixth One UI 9 beta for the Galaxy S26 series. The 851MB update (firmware ZZHE) includes the August 5, 2026, security patch and fixes key issues, including display errors with the Now Brief widget and photo-saving issues in Expert RAW 24MP at specific focal lengths. Currently live in Germany, India, Poland, the UK, and South Korea, the new update will soon be available in the US as well. Samsung entered One UI 9 development with much gusto, but after releasing the stable update alongside the new Galaxy Z8 foldables, the pace of One UI 9 beta releases for its previous flagships has slowed down a bit. After releasing the fifth One UI 9 beta almost two weeks ago, Samsung is now picking things up with the sixth One UI 9 beta release for the Galaxy S26 series. We’ve received the sixth One UI 9 update on our Galaxy S26 Ultra in the UK. This Android 17-based update comes with firmware version ending in ZZHE, the August 5, 2026 security patch, and is 851MB in size.

title: 5 reasons I may not go back to Spotify after trying YouTube Music
summary: YouTube Music isn't perfect, but you can't ignore the value proposition.
body: As is the case with millions of users around the world, I’ve been a loyal Spotify subscriber for as long as I can remember. The app works well across Android and iOS, there’s a great selection of music, and features like Jam and Spotify Connect have made my listening experience much more seamless across audio devices at home. I was happy to pay for the Premium Duo plan — until it was sneakily taken away. Spotify removed the Duo plan in India around November 2025, but as I had subscribed to it long before, I was able to continue with it, as it should be. Then came the email, one July morning this year, saying my Premium Duo plan was canceled due to an “issue” with my payment method. Nothing had changed, so it didn’t make any sense. I figured it was Spotify forcing me to upgrade to a higher-priced plan, and as it turned out, I wasn’t the only one who got the boot. Frustrated with this move, I decided to try other options.

title: Google Home made users say the weirdest thing to set an alarm, but that’s over now
summary: It's a small fix, but a welcome one for anyone who relies on voice alarms daily.
body: TL;DR Some Google Home devices stopped setting alarms via voice command for several days. The bug hit both Google Assistant and Gemini for Home, affecting Nest speakers, displays, and even third-party devices like Lenovo smart displays. Google has confirmed the fix, and our own testing shows alarms are setting and triggering correctly again. Google Home has had a busy August, with Google rolling out several updates that make Gemini for Home smarter and add new capabilities to its smart home platform. But amid all those improvements, something as basic as setting an alarm suddenly stopped working for some users. Thankfully, Google has now confirmed that the issue affecting Nest and other Gemini-powered smart home devices has been fixed. For several days, users on Reddit reported that commands such as “Hey Google, set an alarm for 8:30 AM” would simply be ignored. Some found that alarms worked when set for an exact hour, while others had to ask Google to set an alarm first and then provide the time when prompted. One odd workaround involved saying “Hey Google, hi” before giving the alarm command.

title: The Pixel 11 Pro’s camera flash is a ‘LoLight’ thanks to HiLight
summary: Users complain that the Pixel 11 Pro's camera flash is a big downgrade over other phones, and HiLight could be to blame here.
body: Credit: Sanuj Bhatia / Android Authority TL;DR Reddit users report that the Google Pixel 11 Pro’s camera flash is significantly weaker than that of older Pixels and competitors. Our preliminary testing here at Android Authority shows the Pixel 11 Pro XL torch mode registered 89 lux compared to 123 lux on the Pixel 10 Pro XL. The physical diffuser added to the camera visor for the new HiLight LED array is likely the cause of the softer beam. Google’s new Pixel 11 Pro series introduces HiLight , a small array of ambient LEDs around the camera flash that give you some bits of information without requiring you to turn over or unlock your phone. Google ended up severely limiting HiLight’s functionality, and users had to resort to apps like HiLight Studio to unlock the LED’s full potential. As it turns out, Google gimped HiLight in more ways than one, with the LED flash itself also downgraded compared to the Pixel 10 series. Reddit user pcman2000 voiced their frustration with the Pixel 11 Pro’s camera flash, calling it “really weak” and the weakest among all the phones they tested, ranking it below the Pixel 9 Pro and even the iPhone 17e.

title: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has a camera problem, and it has nothing to do with photo quality
summary: Samsung put the Galaxy Z Fold 8's folding display selfie camera in the worst spot.
body: I’ve spent years trying the latest book-style foldables, but none earned a permanent spot in my pocket once I finished testing them. Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 7 came the closest with a thin-and-light design and truly flagship specs. Unfortunately, it suffered from the same problems as every other folding phone with a squarish inner screen aspect ratio. The form factor isn’t conducive to widescreen video content, as you’ll see large black bars at the top and bottom of the folding screen. Samsung built the wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 to specifically address this pain point, and it quickly won me over. Then, something happened that I didn’t expect. I found myself using the Galaxy Z Fold 8 unfolded in portrait orientation more than landscape.

Quick Share made an unexpected leap beyond Android last year when Google made it compatible with Apple’s AirDrop . Nelson calls the Pixel 11 Pro XL “one of the easiest phones to repair of 2026.” It looks like it should be relatively easy to make the Pixel 11 Pro last. The XL version has now undergone the JerryRigEverything treatment, and the phone held up nicely to Zack Nelson’s usual battery of abuse. The teardown video also shows that common repairs should be relatively simple, with both the display and the battery removable with just a few minutes of work. YouTube’s interface has become something of a moving target lately. The company was only recently testing a new button arrangement on Android that removed text labels from the controls under videos. And now, a small change to how YouTube shows skipped time appears to be rolling out to some Android users. The change involves YouTube’s familiar double-tap gesture for skipping. This broke popular use cases for using Now Playing’s notifications to import songs into apps, such as Last.fm. What followed was dissatisfaction from users, which Google is now looking to address. It is working to add notifications for the currently playing track back to the app with a future update.

summary: You can still block ads — just not how you used to.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority A few years ago, Chrome introduced Manifest V3 and began phasing out the older Manifest V2 technology used by some of the most advanced browser extensions. title: Nintendo just went nuclear on Switch emulators (again)
summary: Nintendo just can't stand Switch games running on anything other than a Switch.
body: TL;DR Nintendo has filed seven new DMCA notices taking down over 400 GitHub repositories related to Switch emulators. The notice took down repos for emulators such as Suyu, Skyline, and several others. It’s no secret that Nintendo has historically taken an extremely strict stance against emulators and people using its IP without permission. A few months ago, the company sent DMCA notices to take down several Switch emulators whose code was hosted on GitHub. Now, the company has thrown another proverbial Donkey Kong barrel at more such GitHub repositories. Nintendo has filed seven DMCA complaints with GitHub to take down over 400 repositories related to Switch emulators in a single day (via TorrentFreak ). This includes emulators like Suyu, which gained popularity after the Yuzu emulator shut down in 2024. According to the DMCA notice displayed publicly on the Suyu repository, GitHub took down all 311 repositories in the network due to Nintendo’s DMCA notice.
